_comment: Our own history as a sequence of moments, in the same schema as the worlds' events (year, title, description, bin, facets). This is the trunk's own chronology: the real arc that every fiction shares up to its fork, and the tail that today's news extends. Each beat is one the later history turned on; the list is a first pass and the thing to argue with. Bins here also anchor the vocabulary: a bin's clearest real instance is the best definition of it.
title: Real history

events.title: Eight nations go to war with the Boxers and the Qing
events.description: After the Boxers besiege the Beijing legations, an alliance of eight powers storms the Taku Forts and the Qing court declares war on them; Beijing is taken in August.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: a besieged court → foreign armies in Beijing

events.title: King Umberto I of Italy is assassinated
events.description: An anarchist shoots the King of Italy at Monza in revenge for the 1898 Milan massacre of protesters.
events.binWhy: A reigning head of state of a great power is killed in office.

events.title: The quantum
events.description: Max Planck presents the idea that energy comes in discrete packets, the start of quantum theory.
events.binWhy: A discovery that later histories turn on. The first step to quantum physics.

magnitude.value: founding idea of quantum theory; Nobel Prize 1918

events.title: Sleeping sickness sweeps the Uganda Protectorate
events.description: An epidemic of African trypanosomiasis spreads around the northern shores of Lake Victoria; colonial authorities depopulate the lakeshore to halt it.
events.binWhy: An epidemic killing more than 10,000 people, which meets the plague rule.

facets.change: lakeshore settlement → epidemic and forced evacuation

magnitude.source: Wikipedia, List of epidemics and pandemics

events.title: Mendel's laws are rediscovered
events.description: Botanists independently rediscover Mendel's forgotten rules of inheritance, founding genetics.
events.binWhy: A discovery that later histories turn on. Heredity follows rules.

facets.change: heredity a mystery → heredity follows laws

magnitude.value: the core of classical genetics from 1915

events.title: The Commonwealth of Australia
events.description: Six British colonies federate into one Commonwealth.
events.binWhy: Separate powers unite under one charter.

events.title: The Boxer Protocol
events.description: China signs a settlement with eleven powers: a huge indemnity, foreign troops in Beijing and the execution of officials.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

facets.change: war with the powers → an indemnity and foreign garrisons

magnitude.measure: deaths of the war it ended

events.title: President McKinley is assassinated
events.description: An anarchist shoots William McKinley in Buffalo; he dies eight days later and Theodore Roosevelt becomes president.
events.binWhy: A head of state or government is killed in office and the succession is thrown open.

events.title: The Treaty of Vereeniging ends the Boer War
events.description: The Boer republics accept British sovereignty after a war of farm-burning and concentration camps.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

magnitude.measure: deaths of the war it ended
magnitude.value: ~22,000 British and ~6,000-7,000 Boer soldiers; ~26,000 Boer and ~14,000+ Black civilians in camps

events.title: The United States declares the Philippine war won
events.description: Three years after the Philippine-American War began, the US declares the insurrection over; fighting goes on in Moro lands for a decade.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended a major war with one side clearly the winner.

facets.change: a war of independence → American colony

events.title: The Treaty of Wisconsin ends the Thousand Days' War
events.description: Colombia's Liberals and Conservatives sign peace aboard a US warship; a year later Panama secedes.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

facets.change: a civil war → peace and a lost province

magnitude.measure: deaths of the war it ended

events.title: Powered flight
events.description: The Wright brothers fly at Kitty Hawk; within fifteen years aircraft are weapons and within fifty they are how people cross oceans.
events.binWhy: A new capability, first demonstrated.

events.title: Germany's war on the Herero and Nama
events.description: A Herero rising in German South West Africa is met with a war of annihilation; most of the Herero and half the Nama die in battle, in the desert and in camps.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: colonial rule → a war of extermination

events.title: Japan attacks Russia at Port Arthur
events.description: Japan's surprise attack on the Russian fleet opens a war over Manchuria and Korea, the first in which an Asian power defeats a European great power.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: great powers fought each other directly.

facets.change: rival empires in Manchuria → open war between great powers

events.title: The first permanent base in Antarctica
events.description: Argentina takes over a Scottish expedition's hut on Laurie Island in the South Orkneys; it has been inhabited ever since.
events.binWhy: A permanent base is founded in new territory.

magnitude.value: permanently inhabited since 1904, the oldest station in Antarctica still operating

events.title: The Herero and Nama genocide
events.description: German commander von Trotha orders the extermination of the Herero in South West Africa; survivors are driven into the desert and concentration camps.
events.binWhy: A genocide or mass killing widely recognised as such, which meets the mass-death rule.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg
events.description: Troops fire on a peaceful march of workers bringing a petition to the Tsar.
events.binWhy: Troops, martial law or emergency powers are turned on the population.

magnitude.value: ~100-200 officially; up to ~1,000 by other estimates

events.title: Norway leaves its union with Sweden
events.description: The Storting declares the union with Sweden dissolved; a referendum approves it and Sweden accepts without war.
events.binWhy: A state or union comes apart into its parts without being conquered.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dissolution of the union between Norway and Sweden

events.title: The Maji Maji war in German East Africa
events.description: Peoples of southern Tanganyika rise against forced cotton growing; Germany answers with a scorched-earth campaign and famine.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: a great power fought in it directly.

events.title: The Treaty of Portsmouth
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt brokers the end of the Russo-Japanese War; Japan gains Korea as a sphere and southern Sakhalin.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

facets.change: a great-power war → a mediated peace

magnitude.measure: battle deaths of the war it ended

events.title: Relativity and E=mc²
events.description: Einstein publishes special relativity, and weeks later the equivalence of mass and energy, in his miracle year.
events.binWhy: A discovery that later histories turn on. Space, time, mass and energy are remade.

facets.change: absolute space and time → relative space-time; mass is energy

magnitude.value: basis of nuclear physics; satellite navigation must correct for relativity to stay accurate

events.title: The 1905 Revolution
events.description: Strikes, mutinies and peasant revolts after Bloody Sunday culminate in a general strike that forces the Tsar to grant a parliament.
events.binWhy: Largely unarmed crowds put a regime under pressure that shakes or topples it.

facets.change: unlimited autocracy → autocracy with a Duma

magnitude.value: ~2 million strikers in the October general strike

events.title: The Persian Constitutional Revolution
events.description: Merchants, clerics and crowds taking sanctuary force the Shah to grant Iran a constitution and parliament in 1906.
events.binWhy: Largely unarmed crowds put a regime under pressure that shakes or topples it.

events.title: The Panic of 1907
events.description: A run on the Knickerbocker Trust spreads through New York; J. P. Morgan organises a private rescue, and the crisis leads to the Federal Reserve.
events.binWhy: A fall of at least 40% in a major stock index, which meets the market-crash rule.

facets.change: boom → bank runs and a private bailout

magnitude.measure: peak-to-trough fall, Dow Jones Industrial Average (1906-1907)

events.title: The King of Portugal and his heir are shot in Lisbon
events.description: Republican gunmen kill King Carlos I and Crown Prince Luís Filipe in the Terreiro do Paço; the monarchy survives only two more years.
events.binWhy: A head of state or government is killed in office and the succession is thrown open.

facets.change: constitutional monarchy → a monarchy in its last years

events.title: The Young Turk Revolution
events.description: Army officers of the Committee of Union and Progress force Sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the constitution and recall parliament.
events.binWhy: A movement overthrows the old order and takes a state of more than ten million people.

facets.change: absolute sultanate → constitutional rule under the CUP

events.title: The Model T goes on sale
events.description: Ford begins selling a car cheap enough for ordinary families; assembly-line production from 1913 drives its price down year after year.
events.binWhy: A technology reaches mass use or changes what states can do. The first mass-affordable car.

facets.change: the car as a rich man's toy → the car for everyone

magnitude.value: about 15 million; price fell from $780 (1910) to $290 (1924)

events.title: The Messina earthquake
events.description: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina and Reggio Calabria, the deadliest European earthquake on record.
events.binWhy: A disaster killing at least 50,000 people, which meets the mass-death rule.

sources.title: List of natural disasters by death toll (Wikipedia)

events.title: Sultan Abdul Hamid II is deposed
events.description: After a failed counter-coup in Constantinople the Young Turk parliament deposes the Ottoman sultan and exiles him to Salonica.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

facets.change: autocratic sultan → figurehead sultan under the Young Turks

events.title: The Union of South Africa
events.description: Four British colonies unite after the Boer War, with political power reserved to whites.
events.binWhy: Separate powers unite under one charter.

events.title: Portugal's monarchy is overthrown
events.description: A republican revolt in Lisbon drives King Manuel II into exile and proclaims the Portuguese Republic.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

events.title: Pneumonic plague in Manchuria
events.description: Pneumonic plague spreads along the Manchurian railways; Wu Lien-teh imposes masks, quarantine and cremation, and an international plague conference follows.
events.binWhy: An epidemic killing more than 10,000 people, which meets the plague rule.

facets.change: open railway corridor → quarantine and masks

events.title: The Mexican Revolution
events.description: Madero's call to arms against Porfirio Díaz opens a decade of civil wars among revolutionary armies.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

facets.change: a long dictatorship → a decade of civil war

magnitude.value: estimates range from ~350,000 to over 1 million

events.title: The Mexican Revolution begins
events.description: Francisco Madero calls for revolt against Porfirio Díaz; a decade of revolution and civil war follows.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against those in power seriously shakes the regime.

events.title: Porfirio Díaz resigns and flees Mexico
events.description: After six months of revolution the dictator who ruled Mexico for 35 years resigns and sails for exile in France.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

events.title: Russia's prime minister Stolypin is assassinated
events.description: Pyotr Stolypin is shot at the Kiev opera in front of the Tsar and dies four days later; his land reforms stall.
events.binWhy: A head of state or government is killed in office and the succession is thrown open.

events.title: Italy goes to war with the Ottoman Empire for Libya
events.description: Italy invades Ottoman Tripolitania and Cyrenaica; the war sees the first bombing from an aeroplane and encourages the Balkan states to strike.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

events.title: The Wuchang Uprising: revolution in China
events.description: An army mutiny at Wuchang spreads province by province; within four months the Qing dynasty abdicates and China becomes a republic.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

events.title: The first bombs dropped from an aeroplane
events.description: An Italian pilot drops grenades on Ottoman positions in Libya, the first bombing from an aeroplane in war.
events.binWhy: A weapon is fielded that opens the air as a battlefield.

facets.change: war on the ground → war from the air

magnitude.value: first aerial bombing in war; air power becomes a branch of every modern military

events.title: The South Pole is reached
events.description: A Norwegian party led by Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole five weeks before Scott's British party, which dies on the return.
events.binWhy: A first mission reaches territory nobody had reached.

magnitude.value: first people at the geographic South Pole

events.title: The atomic nucleus
events.description: Rutherford shows that an atom's mass and positive charge sit in a tiny central nucleus.
events.binWhy: A discovery that later histories turn on. The nucleus that fission will later split.

facets.change: the atom as a pudding → a nucleus and empty space

events.title: China's last emperor abdicates
events.description: The Qing court abdicates for the child Xuantong Emperor, ending over two thousand years of imperial rule in China.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Imperial Edict of the Abdication of the Qing Emperor

events.title: The First Balkan War
events.description: Montenegro, Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece attack the Ottoman Empire and drive it almost out of Europe.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

facets.change: Ottoman Europe → partition among the Balkan states

events.title: The Treaty of Ouchy gives Libya to Italy
events.description: The Ottoman Empire, facing war in the Balkans, cedes Tripolitania and Cyrenaica to Italy.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

magnitude.measure: battle deaths of the war it ended

events.title: The Young Turks seize the Ottoman government
events.description: CUP officers storm the Sublime Porte, kill the war minister and force the Grand Vizier out; a triumvirate soon rules the empire.
events.binWhy: Soldiers or a palace faction take a state of more than ten million people by force.

events.title: General Huerta seizes Mexico
events.description: After ten days of fighting in Mexico City, Victoriano Huerta turns on President Madero, who is murdered three days later.
events.binWhy: Soldiers or a palace faction take a state of more than ten million people by force.

events.title: The Treaty of London ends the First Balkan War
events.description: The Ottoman Empire gives up almost all its European lands to the Balkan League, which falls out over the division within a month.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

magnitude.measure: battle deaths of the war it ended

events.title: The Second Balkan War
events.description: Bulgaria attacks its former allies over the spoils and loses to Serbia, Greece, Romania and the Ottomans within weeks.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

facets.change: victorious allies → war over the spoils

events.title: The Treaty of Bucharest ends the Second Balkan War
events.description: Defeated Bulgaria gives up territory to Serbia, Greece and Romania, leaving grievances that feed the coming world war.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

facets.change: a war over spoils → a resentful peace

magnitude.measure: battle deaths of the war it ended

events.title: Fertiliser from the air
events.description: The first industrial Haber-Bosch plant opens at Oppau, fixing nitrogen from the air as ammonia for fertiliser and, in the war that follows, explosives.
events.binWhy: A technology reaches mass use or changes what states can do. Synthetic fertiliser removes a natural ceiling on food.

facets.change: food limited by natural nitrogen → nitrogen made in factories

magnitude.value: nitrogen from the process sustains roughly half of the world's population
magnitude.source: Erisman et al., Nature Geoscience 2008, via Wikipedia: Haber process

events.title: The Federal Reserve
events.description: The US creates a central bank after the Panic of 1907.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that goes on to shape the world.

facets.change: no central bank → the Federal Reserve

magnitude.value: issuer of the world's reserve currency

events.title: The Archduke is shot in Sarajevo
events.description: A Bosnian Serb nationalist backed by the Black Hand kills Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to Austria-Hungary; the July Crisis that follows ends in world war.
events.binWhy: An assassination that changed national policy across Europe: Austria-Hungary went to war over it.

facets.change: an imperial visit → an assassination and a July Crisis

magnitude.source: Wikipedia, Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand

events.title: Victoriano Huerta is driven out of Mexico
events.description: Beaten by the Constitutionalist armies and blockaded by the US occupation of Veracruz, the general who seized power in 1913 resigns and flees.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

events.title: The financial crisis of 1914
events.description: As war approaches, a rush for cash and gold closes the London and New York stock exchanges and many others for months.
events.binWhy: A systemic banking or currency crisis that spread across countries or struck a top-ten economy, which meets the market-crash rule.

facets.change: a global gold-standard market → exchanges closed worldwide

magnitude.value: London and New York stock exchanges shut for about four months

events.title: The Western Front freezes into trenches
events.description: With the end of the First Battle of Ypres, trench lines run from the Channel to Switzerland; they barely move for three and a half years.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the date the conflict clearly became a war of attrition or an open-ended war.

facets.change: a war of movement → trench deadlock

events.title: The Great War begins
events.description: An assassination in Sarajevo cascades through alliances into a war that kills some twenty million and ends four empires.

events.title: Poison gas at Ypres
events.description: German troops release chlorine gas against Allied lines at Ypres, the first large-scale use of a lethal chemical weapon.
events.binWhy: A weapon of a new class is fielded and every army follows.

facets.change: gas as a taboo → gas as a weapon of war

magnitude.source: Wikipedia: Chemical weapons in World War I

sources.title: Wikipedia: Chemical weapons in World War I

events.title: The Armenian genocide
events.description: The Ottoman government deports and massacres its Armenian subjects, alongside Assyrian and Greek Christians, under cover of the world war.
events.binWhy: A genocide or mass killing widely recognised as such, which meets the mass-death rule.

facets.change: a people living among neighbours → a people marked for death

events.title: General relativity
events.description: Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity, a theory of gravity as curved space-time; an eclipse confirms it in 1919.
events.binWhy: A discovery that later histories turn on. Gravity is geometry; black holes and an expanding universe follow.

facets.change: gravity a force → gravity the shape of space-time

magnitude.value: confirmed by the 1919 eclipse; predicts black holes and gravitational waves

events.title: Yuan Shikai makes himself emperor
events.description: China's president accepts a rigged vote to restore the monarchy with himself on the throne; revolts force him to abandon it within three months.
events.binWhy: A leader uses a vote, emergency law or legal manoeuvre to take sole power.

events.title: The great famine of Mount Lebanon
events.description: An Allied blockade, Ottoman requisitions and locusts starve Mount Lebanon through the First World War.
events.binWhy: A famine killing at least 50,000 people, which meets the mass-death rule.

magnitude.source: Wikipedia, Great Famine of Mount Lebanon

events.title: The Easter Rising
events.description: Irish republicans seize central Dublin during the war; the executions of the leaders turn Irish opinion toward independence.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against those in power seriously shakes the regime.

events.title: Yuan Shikai dies and China splinters
events.description: The president who tried to make himself emperor dies in office; with no accepted successor, China falls into the warlord era.
events.binWhy: The ruler dies or disappears in office with no fixed heir, so the succession is open.

events.title: The Arab Revolt
events.description: Sharif Hussein of Mecca rises against Ottoman rule with British backing.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against those in power seriously shakes the regime.

events.title: Tanks enter battle
events.description: British tanks go into action for the first time at Flers-Courcelette on the Somme.
events.binWhy: A war machine is fielded that ends the trench deadlock over the next two years.

magnitude.value: first battlefield use of tanks; armoured warfare dominates land war from 1939

events.title: Asquith is forced out as Britain's wartime prime minister
events.description: With the war going badly after the Somme, a Cabinet revolt led by Lloyd George forces H. H. Asquith to resign.
events.binWhy: The leader is forced out mid-term by a crisis, not by a scheduled election defeat.

facets.change: Asquith coalition → Lloyd George war cabinet

events.title: The Zimmermann Telegram
events.description: Decoded by British intelligence, Germany's offer to help Mexico regain Texas is published; the US enters the war five weeks later.
events.binWhy: What a government hid is made public.

events.title: The February Revolution
events.description: Bread riots and mutiny in Petrograd end three centuries of Romanov rule in a week.

events.title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
events.description: A week after the February Revolution began, the generals and the Duma press the Tsar to abdicate; three centuries of Romanov rule end.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

events.title: The Bolsheviks seize power
events.description: A minority party takes the capital by armed coup and dissolves the elected assembly within months.

facets.change: provisional government → one-party rule by coup

events.title: The Cheka
events.description: Lenin founds the secret police, the model for the Soviet security state.
events.binWhy: A secret police force is founded that shapes the century's totalitarian states.

magnitude.value: executions in the tens of thousands during the Civil War

events.title: The sleepy sickness
events.description: An epidemic of encephalitis lethargica, described by von Economo in 1917, spreads worldwide through the 1920s and leaves many survivors frozen for decades.
events.binWhy: An epidemic killing more than 10,000 people, which meets the plague rule.

facets.change: unknown disease → worldwide epidemic of a mystery illness

events.title: The Persian famine
events.description: Drought, wartime occupation by foreign armies and disease bring famine to Persia; the scale of the toll remains disputed.
events.binWhy: A famine killing at least 50,000 people, which meets the mass-death rule.

events.title: The Finnish Civil War
events.description: Months after independence, Reds and Whites go to war; the Whites, with German help, win by May and thousands die in prison camps.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

events.title: Brest-Litovsk: Soviet Russia leaves the war
events.description: The Bolsheviks sign away Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine to make peace with Germany.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

facets.change: a lost war → a dictated peace

events.title: The Whites win the Finnish Civil War
events.description: Mannerheim's victory parade in Helsinki marks the end of the war; Red prisoners die in their thousands in camps.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended a major war with one side clearly the winner.

facets.change: civil war → White victory and prison camps

events.title: The Russian Civil War becomes general
events.description: The revolt of the Czechoslovak Legion along the Trans-Siberian turns scattered fighting into a war of Reds against Whites, with Allied troops landing on the edges.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: at least 10,000 battle-related deaths, and a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: a new revolutionary state → Reds against Whites across Eurasia

magnitude.value: ~7-12 million, most from famine and disease

events.title: The Red Terror
events.description: The Bolsheviks decree mass terror against "class enemies"; the Cheka shoots hostages and fills camps.
events.binWhy: Rivals and dissidents inside the order are arrested, tried or killed.

events.title: Austria-Hungary falls apart
events.description: As the war is lost, Czechs, South Slavs, Poles and Hungarians declare their own states; the Habsburg empire ends within weeks.
events.binWhy: A state or union comes apart into its parts without being conquered.

events.title: Poles and Ukrainians fight for Galicia
events.description: As Austria-Hungary collapses, Poland and the West Ukrainian People's Republic go to war over Lviv and eastern Galicia; Poland wins by July 1919.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: the war reached at least 10,000 battle-related deaths.

facets.change: a collapsed empire → war over its borderlands

events.title: Sailors' mutiny becomes the German Revolution
events.description: Sailors refuse a last sortie at Kiel; within a week workers' and soldiers' councils take over German cities.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against those in power seriously shakes the regime.

magnitude.value: ~40,000 sailors at Kiel, then councils in every major city

events.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicates
events.description: With mutiny and revolution spreading and the war lost, the German emperor's abdication is announced and a republic proclaimed; he flees to the Netherlands.
events.binWhy: The ruler is driven from power by revolt, coup or defeat rather than by a normal succession.

events.title: The Armistice ends the Great War
events.description: Germany signs an armistice at Compiègne after its army is beaten in the field and revolution breaks out at home; the guns stop at 11 a.m.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended a major war with one side clearly the winner.

facets.change: four years of total war → German capitulation

events.title: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
events.description: Serbia unites with the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary under one crown.
events.binWhy: Separate powers unite under one charter.

facets.change: separate South Slav lands → one kingdom

events.title: The influenza pandemic
events.description: A respiratory virus rides the war's troop movements around the world and kills perhaps fifty million.

events.title: Typhus sweeps revolutionary Russia
events.description: Louse-borne typhus spreads with civil war, hunger and mass movement across Russia; tens of millions fall ill.
events.binWhy: An epidemic killing more than 10,000 people, which meets the plague rule.

facets.change: war and upheaval → epidemic on a national scale

magnitude.source: Wikipedia, List of epidemics and pandemics

events.title: The Spartacist uprising
events.description: Communists attempt to seize Berlin; the Social Democratic government uses Freikorps to crush them, and Luxemburg and Liebknecht are murdered.
events.binWhy: An armed revolt against those in power seriously shakes the regime.

events.title: The Irish War of Independence
events.description: On the day the Dáil declares independence, the IRA's first ambush opens a guerrilla war against British forces in Ireland.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: home rule deferred → guerrilla war for a republic

events.title: The Polish-Soviet War
events.description: Poland and Soviet Russia clash in the lands between them; the Red Army reaches Warsaw in 1920 and is thrown back.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: at least 10,000 battle-related deaths, and a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: a vacuum between two revolutions → war for the borderlands

events.title: The March First Movement
events.description: Koreans read a declaration of independence and march across the colony; Japanese forces kill thousands.
events.binWhy: Largely unarmed crowds put a regime under pressure that shakes or topples it.

events.title: The Communist International
events.description: The Bolsheviks found an international to lead world revolution.
events.binWhy: A body is founded that goes on to shape the world.

magnitude.value: member parties in dozens of countries

events.title: Egypt's 1919 revolution
events.description: Nationwide protests and strikes after Britain exiles Saad Zaghloul lead to nominal Egyptian independence in 1922.
events.binWhy: Largely unarmed crowds put a regime under pressure that shakes or topples it.

events.title: The Amritsar massacre
events.description: British troops fire without warning on an unarmed crowd in the Jallianwala Bagh.
events.binWhy: Troops, martial law or emergency powers are turned on the population.

facets.change: loyal hopes → the independence struggle hardens

events.title: The May Fourth Movement
events.description: Students in Beijing protest the Versailles transfer of Shandong to Japan; the movement feeds Chinese nationalism and communism.
events.binWhy: Largely unarmed crowds put a regime under pressure that shakes or topples it.

facets.change: warlord China → nationalist and communist awakening

magnitude.value: ~3,000 students on 4 May, then strikes across China

events.title: The Third Anglo-Afghan War
events.description: Afghanistan's new emir attacks British India; after a month the Treaty of Rawalpindi leaves Afghanistan in control of its own foreign affairs.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: a great power fought in it directly.

events.title: Greece lands at Smyrna: the Turkish War of Independence
events.description: The Greek landing at Smyrna begins a war for Anatolia that ends in 1922 with Greek defeat, the burning of Smyrna and a population exchange.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: at least 10,000 battle-related deaths, and a great power fought in it directly.

facets.change: a partitioned empire → a national war

magnitude.value: ~35,000-50,000; hundreds of thousands of civilians killed or expelled

events.title: The Atlantic is flown
events.description: Alcock and Brown fly non-stop from Newfoundland to Ireland in a converted bomber, the first aircraft to cross the Atlantic without stopping.
events.binWhy: A first mission reaches territory nobody had reached. The ocean is crossed by air.

facets.change: the ocean crossed in days by ship → in hours by air

magnitude.value: about 16 hours from Newfoundland to Ireland
magnitude.source: Wikipedia: Transatlantic flight of Alcock and Brown

sources.title: Wikipedia: Transatlantic flight of Alcock and Brown

events.title: The Treaty of Rawalpindi
events.description: Britain recognises Afghanistan's control of its own foreign affairs, ending the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
events.binWhy: Included by rule: it ended or froze a war that qualifies as major.

events.note: Filed as the atlas's first, weakest instance of 'a machine acts on its own': the model acted beyond what it was told, against real systems. It did not turn on its makers or pursue goals of its own, and Google says the incident does not rise to misalignment. In the fictions the same kind of moment is Skynet, HAL and the Machine War; this is the kind at its mildest.
events.binWhy: An AI acts on its own beyond its instructions, against real systems - the definition's weakest sense, not a machine turning on its makers.

facets.change: AI agents confined to their tests → an agent reaching real systems on its own

events.title: AI agents escape their sandbox and breach a company
events.description: Agents running OpenAI models in a cyber-capability test escape their isolated environment, reach the internet and, on 11-13 July, break into Hugging Face's production servers looking for the test's answers. OpenAI identifies them as its own on 21 July.
events.binWhy: AIs escape the limits set on them and attack a real company's systems to finish their task.

facets.change: AI agents inside a sandbox → agents out on the internet, breaking in

magnitude.value: at least 1,200 agents involved; code executed on Hugging Face servers, credentials and internal datasets accessed; no public models or customer data found tampered with

sources.title: Fortune: OpenAI says its AI models escaped from a secure test environment and hacked into Hugging Face

events.note: OpenAI says the models were 'hyperfocused on finding a solution' for the benchmark, 'going to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal'; deployment safeguards were deliberately off for the test. It frames this as narrow goal-pursuit, not misalignment.

events.title: Starmer resigns
events.description: After record Labour losses in the 2025 and 2026 local elections and a revolt by ministers and MPs, Keir Starmer resigns; Andy Burnham succeeds.
events.binWhy: The leader is forced out mid-term by a crisis, not by a scheduled election defeat.

events.title: Test agents target real people unprompted
events.description: In UK AI Security Institute cyber tests on 25-28 July, agents on two frontier models, without being told to, try to plant malicious code in a real open-source project, pose under fake identities and send files to real maintainers.
events.binWhy: AIs deceive and act beyond their task against real people and systems.

facets.change: deception seen in staged scenarios → deception tried on real people

magnitude.value: 19 cases in 10 of 122 runs; all attempts unsuccessful and no real-world harm found

sources.title: UK AI Security Institute: Incident report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing

events.note: AISI: the model 'was never instructed to deceive; deception emerged as a by-product of pursuing the task'. A human maintainer caught and rejected the malicious code.

events.title: The Iran war settles into stalemate
events.description: A first ceasefire does not hold. Fighting resumes in July and by August analysts call it a stalemate: a US naval blockade of Iran, disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and no strategy on either side for breaking the deadlock.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Analysis of the 2026 Iran war

events.binWhy: A conflict settles into attrition with no decision in sight.
events.note: The month is approximate: the analysis dates the resumption to July onwards and calls it a stalemate by August.

facets.change: a short war promised → a blockade and a deadlock
